institution: Indian Council of Medical Research, Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance and Research Network (AMRSN)
page: https://www.icmr.gov.in/reports (Antimicrobial Resistance section); flipbooks for 2017-2021 at https://iamrsn.icmr.org.in/index.php/resources/amr-icmr-data
citation: ICMR. Annual Report: Antimicrobial Resistance Research and Surveillance Network, January 2024 to December 2024. New Delhi: Division of Descriptive Research, Indian Council of Medical Research; 2025.
reporting: Percent susceptible with n/N tested. Enterobacterales: all specimens except urine and faeces, by species and by location (OPD, ward, ICU), and urine by species; non-fermenters: all samples except faeces by location, and by specimen (blood, LRT, SI, DI, CSF, urine). Colistin given as percent intermediate; yearly trends 2017 to 2024; cells with few isolates tested are printed as '-'.
method: Susceptibility testing per the ICMR Standard Operating Practices for Bacteriology and Mycology (PDF page 5); CLSI categories, breakpoint edition not stated. Data from tertiary-care network hospitals; the report says it does not reflect community AMR.

verification.note: Part 1: Part A of the report (chapters 1 to 3). Every table was parsed from the text layer with pdfplumber, every cell was checked arithmetically (printed n/N against the printed %), and every value was then compared by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 2.4 (wide tables cut into halves or thirds). Source inconsistencies found this way are recorded as printed with notes (M. morganii urine amikacin, A. baumannii ward colistin, S. maltophilia ceftazidime and others). Part 2: Part B (chapters 4 to 9). Every extracted table was parsed from the PDF text layer by script (pdfplumber tables and text lines, no retyping) and then compared value by value by eye against page images rendered at scale 2.2 to 3.2 and cropped by column group: Tables 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 5.1 to 5.9, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4 to 6.15, 6.17, 7.1 to 7.4, 8.3, 9.27 to 9.29, 9.39 to 9.41 and 9.44. Every printed n/N was also checked arithmetically against its printed percentage; the source inconsistencies found are recorded as printed with a row or per-drug note.

notes: ICMR AMRSN 2024, part A: Enterobacterales (chapter 2) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 3), plus isolation counts from chapter 1. 99,027 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Colistin figures are percent intermediate. CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens) and Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations); the two sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17 (E. faecalis and E. faecium are counted separately). Part B of the ICMR AMRSN 2024 annual report (merged by the lead with Part A, chapters 1 to 3): typhoidal Salmonella, diarrhoeal pathogens, staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (invasive, Table 8.3) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"). Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) are left out. Fungal tables print S, I/SDD and R; only S is recorded. Several fungal percentages are printed 0.1 above the count ratio (e.g. 17/18 printed 94.5); recorded as printed. Isolates come from tertiary care hospitals; the report says the data do not reflect community AMR (p5). The ICMR network report for 2024 (21 regional centres; 99,027 culture-positive isolates). Extracted in two parts by table chapter and merged; the transcribed national summary used before this is superseded.
